text:
Colorado arrives with the better underlying game. Over the season, COL generates 3.6 expected goals per 60 minutes (a measure of the quality of chances) and allows 2.56, while PHI sits at 2.21 and 3.57. At five on five, COL has taken 55% of the expected goals in its games and PHI 34%. The model projects 3.42 expected goals for COL tonight against 2.48 for PHI. On special teams, COL's power play creates 0.82 expected goals a game and its penalty kill allows 0.32. PHI is at 0.62 and 0.69, and it takes 4.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays.

The goalie matchup runs against the form. Projected starter Joseph Woll (PHI) is at +4.32 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals a goalie saved beyond what the shots should have produced), but was at -7.44 last season. Projected COL starter Mackenzie Blackwood is at -1.82 this year after +8.01 last year. Woll is 0-3-2 over his last five starts despite that strong work, and PHI's finishing (-8.5 goals against its chances) has cost it more than its play deserves. PHI is also without Travis Konecny and Owen Tippett.

Recent form favors COL, 3-1-1 in its last five with 58% of the expected goals, against PHI's 1-3-1 and 42%. Nathan MacKinnon has a 46% chance to score and an 88% chance at a point, helped by Colorado's top power play. Nazem Kadri has no goals in eight games on 3.2 expected goals, a reason the model sees him as due. For PHI, Trevor Zegras (25% to score) leads the list. Noah Juulsen's return to Philadelphia is a story, though the model doesn't price it.
